chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The world will bend towards us after having been refractory, as the biting she-camel bends towards its young.
Then he recited immediately after that:
And intend We to bestow (Our) favour upon those who were considered weak in the land, and to make them the Imams (guides in faith), and to make them the heirs.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran verse about making the oppressed Imams and heirs mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of a nursing mother to describe the world's eventual gentle submission to the Ahl al-Bayt after a period of harshness, linking this eschatological hope to the divine promise in Surah Al-Qasas. This narration is central to Shia political theology, affirming the rightful leadership of the Imams as the ultimate heirs of the earth who will establish justice after the oppression of the unjust.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 209. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him said:
The world will bend towards us after having been refractory as the biting she-camel bends towards its young.
Then Amīr al-mu’minīn recited the verse:
And intend We to bestow (Our) favour upon those who were considered weak in the land, and to make them the Imams (guides in faith), and to make them the heirs. (Qur’ān, 28:5) [1]
